company: KIT H2T (High Performance Humanoid Technologies Lab)
company_native: Karlsruher Institut für Technologie, Institut für Anthropomatik und Robotik
target_applications: household assistance, eldercare/nursing facilities, learning-from-demonstration research

torso_lift.value: 2-DoF knee/hip kinematic for bowing and torso height adjustment (predecessor ARMAR-6: 40 cm telescopic lift, 152-192 cm)

actuators.value: custom sensor-actuator-controller units (BLDC + gear + torque sensing per joint), torque-controlled, EtherCAT

end_effector.value: 2x underactuated five-finger humanoid hands, 4 DoF, integrated in-hand RGB cameras

sensors_head.value: 3-DoF head with multiple camera systems (stereo + depth); microphones for speech interaction

sensors_wrist_hand.value: 6-axis force/torque sensors in wrists; joint torque sensors; in-hand RGB cameras

compute.value: not published for ARMAR-7 (ARMAR-6: 4 onboard PCs + GTX 1080 GPU, Ubuntu)

software_stack.value: ArmarX open-source cognitive architecture; learning from human demonstration, speech/gesture understanding, on-device privacy claim

safety_compliance.value: none (research); compliant torque control for physical HRI

availability.value: not available; one-off university research platform

deployment_evidence.value: Automatica 2025 + Hannover Messe 2026 live demos (dishwasher unloading, laundry sorting, learning from demonstration); lineage: ARMAR-6 SecondHands demos with Ocado 2018-2020

notes: Dossier also covers lineage: ARMAR-6 (2018, SecondHands/Ocado; 152-192 cm, 160 kg, 10 kg/arm, 1 m/s, 1.824 kWh NiMH, 4 Mecanum wheels) and ARMAR-III (2006 kitchen robot). ARMAR-7 height/weight/payload not yet published.
